title: Introduce lightweight CI orchestrator and repo tooling hygiene
author: Maya Alvarez
release_notes: - Introduces a lightweight CI orchestrator shim for stage-aware workflow routing. - Cleans up legacy lint/test scripts and removes unused devdeps. - Adds a release-safety preflight check to reduce flaky merges.
description: Motivation: Our monolithic CI workflows have grown brittle and slow; long lint/test pipelines and duplicated scripts across repos increase maintenance overhead and merge friction. This PR introduces a lightweight orchestrator shim that standardizes stage-aware routing (fastpath/check/slow) and consolidates common bootstraps while performing repo-tooling hygiene and dependency pruning. Summary of changes: 1) New ci/orchestrator/handler.go + shim scripts that provide a small declarative stage map and load balancing between fastpath and full integration lanes. 2) Replace legacy bash lint bootstraps with a typed Node.js runner (ci/lint-runner) that supports staged sharding and caching. 3) Add a release preflight job (ci/preflight-check) which validates toolchain versions, signed changelog presence, and pinlist drift to prevent silent dependency breaks. 4) Remove unused devDependencies in package.json across repo roots and add a devdep-audit script to CI. 5) Consolidate action inputs and standardize cache keys to reduce flakiness and improve cross-repo reuse. Test plan and verification: - Local unit + integration runs for the orchestrator (go test, node unit tests). - CI smoke lane exercises fastpath and full-lane fallbacks. - Ran dep-audit against current repo state and fixed three transient transitive deps. - Manual release dry-run using the new preflight check. Why this approach: The orchestrator is intentionally lightweight (under 200 LOC for the core decision layer) and designed to be opt-in per repo via a small ci/config.yaml. It reduces duplication while preserving per-repo exceptions. Rollout plan: 1) Apply to redwood monorepo as opt-in on a few high-velocity packages (sdk-python, redwood, redwood-devtools). 2) Monitor presubmit latency and failure rate for two weeks. 3) Flip to default once metrics show >20% reduction in median presubmit latency and <3% regression in flaky test rate. Backwards compatibility: Existing workflows are preserved and the shim falls back to legacy behavior when ci/config.yaml is absent. Linked work: ENG-4821 (orchestrator core), ENG-4823 (presubmit sharding), related to prior dep hygiene efforts. Checklist: - [x] Introduce orchestrator shim and minimal config - [x] Replace bash lint bootstraps with typed runner - [x] Add release preflight job and smoke tests - [x] Remove stale devdeps and add devdep-audit - [x] Update docs/ci.md with rollout guidance Commits: ["init: add lightweight orchestrator shim (core decision layer and handler)", "chore: typed lint-runner + staged-shard integration", "ci: add preflight-check job and scripts", "chore: remove unused devdeps in package.json and add devdep-audit", "docs: document orchestrator opt-in and rollout guide", "test: add smoke CI job for fastpath vs full-lane"]

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice cleanup; can you reduce the default fastpath timeout from 45s to 25s? Fastpath queueing still shows occasional spikes. Maya Alvarez: Good call—lowered to 25s and added a short jitter to avoid thundering herd (see handler.go commit).

Ritika Singh: We should gate the release-preflight to only run on release branches to avoid noisy checks on feature branches. Maya Alvarez: Updated workflow to trigger preflight only on tags and release/* (see fastpath.yml), added opt-in flag in ci/config.yaml.

Owen Park: The typed lint-runner looks great, but can we preserve exit code semantics for existing scripts? Add a compatibility wrapper. Maya Alvarez: Added compatibility wrapper script at ci/lint-runner/compat.sh and tests covering exit codes.
